title: Novel 4-Alkyl-Modified Derivatives of N4-Hydroxycytidine, Thymidine, and 4-Thiothymidine: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of the Antimicrobial Activity
content: The identification and development of novel antimicrobial agents constitutes an urgent priority, as pathogenic microorganisms are increasingly exhibiting resistance to existing therapeutic drugs. To investigate how the nature of lipophilic substituents affects the biological properties of pyrimidine nucleosides bearing extended alkyl substituents at the C4 position of the nucleobase moiety, we designed and synthesized 12 new nucleosides. We employed a general synthetic strategy to obtain S4-/O4-alkyl and N4-alkoxy derivatives. The compounds effectively inhibited the growth of several biodeteriorating fungal and gram-positive bacterial strains, including a drug-resistant strain of Staphylococcus aureus, with activity comparable to that of several antibiotics used in clinical practice. The most promising compounds were N4-alkoxy-2′-deoxy-5-methylcytidines, which also exhibited activity against laboratory strains and clinical isolates of mycobacteria with innate resistance to a wide range of antibacterial drugs. In contrast, S4-alkyl-2′-deoxy-5-methyluridines did not inhibit the growth of the bacteria and molds examined. O4-Alkyl and N4-alkoxy derivatives inhibited the growth of molds isolated from the surfaces of icons in the collection of Old Russian paintings at the State Tretyakov Gallery (Moscow), with efficacy similar to that of antiseptics commonly used to protect works of art. These compounds appear promising for expanding the range of antiseptics used in painting conservation.
